title: Derived supported Kummer continuity for affine regular pairs
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], finite Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], and the canonical Kummer class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], with the bounded-below closed-support adjunction [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction].

Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(Z_a\hookrightarrow V_a)_{a\in I}$ an inverse system of pairs of regular affine Noetherian schemes [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion], with affine transition maps and $\ell$ invertible on each $V_a$. Fix $c\geq0$. Suppose that each $Z_a\hookrightarrow V_a$ is cut out by global regular equations $t_{a,1},\ldots,t_{a,c}$, that every transition pulls these elements back to the corresponding elements, and that the limits $Z=\varprojlim_a Z_a$ and $V=\varprojlim_a V_a$ are regular affine Noetherian schemes with the limiting regular sequence cutting out $Z\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence, def-per-regular-closed-immersion-codimension].

Let $\gamma_a:R\Gamma(Z_a,A)\to R\Gamma_{Z_a}(V_a,A(c))[2c]$ be the derived global supported Kummer map, and define $\gamma$ for the limiting pair in the same way; supported sections mean [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. The $\gamma_a$ form a compatible directed diagram, and there is a canonical commutative square in the derived category $D(A)$ of ordinary $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with both vertical maps isomorphisms:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\varinjlim_a R\Gamma(Z_a,A)&\xrightarrow{\varinjlim\gamma_a}&\varinjlim_a R\Gamma_{Z_a}(V_a,A(c))[2c]\\
\downarrow\scriptstyle\sim&&\downarrow\scriptstyle\sim\\
R\Gamma(Z,A)&\xrightarrow{\gamma}&R\Gamma_Z(V,A(c))[2c].
\end{array}$$
Here the filtered derived colimits are computed by taking degreewise filtered colimits in compatible diagrams of cochain-complex representatives; filtered colimits of $A$-modules are exact, so this specifies their derived meaning. The bottom arrow is the canonical class for the limiting regular sequence, with the same Kummer sign, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of the two objects. In particular, if every $\gamma_a$ is an isomorphism, then so is $\gamma$. No flatness of the transition maps is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI section 2.1 (supported Cartier Kummer construction), Definition 2.3.1 (regular-sequence class) and Proposition 2.2.3.1 (base-change compatibility preserving conormal data). Continuity ingredient: Stacks Project Tag 03Q6, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-directed-colimit-cohomology (ambient, complement and closed schemes). The simultaneous derived-arrow comparison is an agent-formulated statement-only obligation; the exact square is not a verbatim theorem in ILO.

proof.text: Write $W_{a,k}=V(t_{a,1},\ldots,t_{a,k})$, so $W_{a,0}=V_a$ and $W_{a,c}=Z_a$, and $U_a=V_a\setminus Z_a$. Define the corresponding limiting flag and $U=V\setminus Z$. Preserved equations show directly by quotient rings that every flag square is Cartesian. The complement is the finite union of the principal opens $D(t_{a,k})$; these also pull back, and their limits are $D(t_k)$. Thus $U$ is the limit of the $U_a$, and the restricted transition maps are affine, since they are base changes of the affine transitions. All three systems $V_a,Z_a,U_a$ are qcqs: the first two are affine Noetherian, and the third is an open in a Noetherian affine. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], multiplication by $t_{a,k}$ on each preceding quotient is injective, so every $W_{a,k}\hookrightarrow W_{a,k-1}$ is Cartier, likewise at the limit. Intermediate flag schemes need not be regular. Fix an index $a_0$ when using continuity: its upper tail is cofinal, since every finite collection of indices has a common upper bound. A cocone on that tail extends uniquely by passing to such an upper bound; two extensions agree at a further upper bound. This identifies its colimits with those over the original directed set.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.3.1; Cartesian flag and open-complement calculations.

proof.text: For $T_a=V_a,Z_a,U_a$, apply [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity] to the upper tail at $a_0$ and the torsion coefficient sheaf $A(m)$ there. Its pullbacks are the required coefficients by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Step 1 verifies qcqs, affine transitions, and the stated limits. Hence the canonical maps $\varinjlim_a H^r(T_a,A(m))\to H^r(T,A(m))$ are isomorphisms for $r\geq0$. The natural comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] identifies these abelian-sheaf cohomology groups with module-sheaf cohomology. The maps are $A$-linear because section pullback is $A$-linear; a bijective $A$-linear map has an $A$-linear inverse. For $r<0$ both sides vanish, since the coefficients are sheaves in degree zero. Use $m=0$ on $Z_a$ and $m=c$ on $V_a,U_a$.

source.place: Tag 03Q6, lemma-directed-colimit-cohomology; passage to constant-ring module coefficients.

proof.text: Take $B=T=V_a$ and $C=Z_a$ in [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle], with $F=A(c)$. This gives the triangle of supported sections, sections on $V_a$, and sections on $U_a$. The cone and pullback comparison in [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] makes these triangles compatible with every transition and limit map, including forgetting support. Filtered colimits of their cohomology exact sequences are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. Compare this sequence with the limiting one. In the five consecutive terms $H^{r-1}(V)\to H^{r-1}(U)\to H_Z^r(V)\to H^r(V)\to H^r(U)$, all four nonsupported comparison maps are isomorphisms by Step 2. The middle map is injective: a class mapping to zero has zero image in $H^r(V)$, hence comes from $H^{r-1}(U)$; its limiting lift comes from $H^{r-1}(V)$, which can be lifted back and subtracted. It is surjective: lift the ambient image of a supported class; its restriction is zero by injectivity on $H^r(U)$, so lift it from the supported term; correct the difference using surjectivity on $H^{r-1}(U)$. Thus supported continuity holds for every integer $r$. In particular, put $X_a=R\Gamma(Z_a,A)$, $Y_a=R\Gamma_{Z_a}(V_a,A(c))[2c]$ and $X,Y$ for the limits. We have canonical isomorphisms $\alpha^q:\varinjlim H^qX_a\cong H^qX$ and $\beta^q:\varinjlim H^qY_a\cong H^qY$, with $r=q+2c$ for the latter.

source.place: Tags 0A45 (support triangle) and 03Q6; explicit exact-sequence comparison.

proof.text: We now compute the actual class under any one of the Cartesian flag maps $h:T'\to T$ of Step 1. Closed direct image on constant-ring modules is exact and identifies modules on the closed subscheme with modules annihilated by restriction to its open complement, by [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization]. Consequently for a closed $j:C\hookrightarrow T$ and any module $M$ on $C$, $h^{-1}j_*M$ is supported on $C'$; its adjunction unit identifies it with $j'_*j'^{-1}h^{-1}j_*M=j'_*h_C^{-1}M$, using the counit $j^{-1}j_*M\cong M$. This is the canonical exchange, natural in $M$, and exactness applies the same calculation termwise to complexes. For constants it is precisely $b_{h,C}$ of [lem-pur-etale-closed-constant-tensor]: $h^{-1}$ is exact, so the inverse image $A_{T'}\to h^{-1}j_*A_C$ of the surjective unit $A_T\to j_*A_C$ is an epimorphism, and both maps carry it to the unit $A_{T'}\to j'_*A_{C'}$ ($b_{h,C}$ by its statement, the exchange by the triangle identities), hence they agree. The same argument identifies $b_{h,C}$ with the closed exchanges of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] and [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality], which are base-change mates of the same square and also carry unit to unit. Units, counits and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] show that these exchanges paste for successive closed immersions. Twisting closed direct image has the canonical comparison $j_*M\otimes A_T(m)\cong j_*(M\otimes A_C(m))$: trivialize the rank-one coefficient line etale locally, where the comparison is the identity on $j_*M$; these local isomorphisms glue. Rank one and its pullback/tensor compatibilities are supplied by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Tensoring with the line is exact by the same local calculation, so this also gives the derived comparison. These comparisons respect exchange, composition and shifts, as can be checked on the same trivializations and on complexes.

source.place: XVI section 2.1 and Proposition 2.2.3.1; explicit closed-exchange and coefficient identifications.

proof.text:
Let $i_a:Z_a\hookrightarrow V_a$ and write $\phi_a:i_{a*}A_{Z_a}\to A_{V_a}(c)[2c]$ for the transpose of the specified class under [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction]. The regular-sequence formula of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], at $n=1$, expresses this arrow as the following finite composite: push the last Cartier map forward through the preceding closed immersions, then apply the preceding Cartier map twisted and shifted, continuing to the first. This is the transpose of the stated composite of exceptional classes because the units and counits for the composite adjunction are pasted, as in [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]. Step 4 supplies the identifications of the successive direct images and twists. For each factor [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] identifies its inverse image along the corresponding flag map with the new Cartier map. Its hypothesis is exactly that the pulled-back divisor is Cartier, verified in Step 1; no flatness is required. Apply inverse image to the finite composite: its preservation of composition, the exchanges of Step 4, and the factor identities give
$$h^{-1}\phi_a\circ b_{h,Z_a}^{-1}=\phi_b.$$
The same calculation applies to a projection from the limit, yielding $\phi$ on $V$. This proves the required nonflat compatibility rather than taking it from the flat-base-change clause of the class-calculus node. There is no additional sign: every factor is its positive Cartier Kummer map. For $c=0$ the composite is the identity on $A$ and the same equation holds.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.3.1, Theorem 2.3.2 and Proposition 2.2.3.1; finite Cartier-factor computation.

proof.text:
For $q\geq0$, represent $x\in H^q(Z_a,A)$ by $x:A_{Z_a}\to A_{Z_a}[q]$ using [lem-weil-pbc-free-sheaf-derived-sections]. Under the supported-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], the operation induced by the class has the explicit formula
$$\Phi( H^q(\gamma_a)(x))=\phi_a[q]\circ i_{a*}x.$$
Indeed the adjunction transpose of the class is $\phi_a$, so applying it to $x$ and then transposing is this composition, by the unit/counit formulas of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction]. For a transition or projection $h$, [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] says that pullback of this supported element is represented by $h^{-1}(\phi_a[q]\,i_{a*}x)b^{-1}$. Naturality of the exchange from Step 4 rewrites it as $(h^{-1}\phi_a\,b^{-1})[q]\,i'_*h_Z^{-1}x$. Step 5 identifies the first factor with $\phi'[q]$. This is the displayed formula for $H^q(\gamma')(h_Z^*x)$, with the same supported-Hom normalization. For $q<0$ the source $H^q(Z_a,A)$ vanishes. Write $u_{ba},v_{ba}$ for the ordinary and supported transitions on $X_a,Y_a$, and $u_a,v_a$ for the limiting legs. We have now proved for every integer $q$ both
$$H^q(v_{ba})H^q(\gamma_a)=H^q(\gamma_b)H^q(u_{ba}),\qquad H^q(v_a)H^q(\gamma_a)=H^q(\gamma)H^q(u_a).$$

source.place: XVI section 2.1, supported-Hom interpretation and Proposition 2.2.3.1; explicit operation calculation.

proof.text: The field hypothesis is decisive. Since $A=\mathbf F_\ell$ with $\ell$ prime, [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(P,Q)\cong\prod_q\operatorname{Hom}_A(H^qP,H^qQ)$ for arbitrary, possibly unbounded and infinite-dimensional, $P,Q$. Apply its injectivity to the two equations of Step 6 for all $q$. This proves $v_{ba}\gamma_a=\gamma_bu_{ba}$ and $v_a\gamma_a=\gamma u_a$ as equalities of the actual arrows in $D(A)$. Thus the $\gamma_a$ are a morphism of directed diagrams and their pullback legs give a cone to the actual $\gamma$. This argument uses the injectivity clause of the Hom bijection, not merely detection of isomorphisms by cohomology.

source.place: field_complex_cohomology_splitting: unrestricted canonical Hom bijection; application to the equations of Step 6.

proof.text: For any $P\in D(A)$ define $S(P)$ explicitly as the complex with term $H^q(P)$ in degree $q$ and zero differential. By the surjectivity of the same Hom bijection there is a unique $\theta_P:Q S(P)\to P$ inducing the identity on every $H^q$ (with the canonical cohomology of a zero-differential complex). Lift the inverse identity family to obtain an inverse: injectivity makes both composites identities. For $f:P\to P'$ let $S(f)^q=H^q(f)$. Functoriality of cohomology gives a strict chain-map functor $S$, and injectivity gives $f\theta_P=\theta_{P'}Q S(f)$. Consequently $S(X_a),S(Y_a)$, with the degreewise maps $H^q(u_{ba}),H^q(v_{ba})$ and $H^q(\gamma_a)$, are compatible diagrams of complex representatives of the original directed arrow diagram. Include $S(X),S(Y)$ and their pullback legs. Step 7 makes all of these squares commute strictly degree by degree. No choices of vector-space complements enter $S$, $\theta$, or these chain maps.

source.place: Unrestricted canonical Hom bijection; explicit zero-differential complex and uniqueness argument.

proof.text: Take degreewise filtered colimits of these strict diagrams, obtaining zero-differential complexes $L_X^q=\varinjlim_aH^q(X_a)$ and $L_Y^q=\varinjlim_aH^q(Y_a)$ and the chain map $g^q=\varinjlim_aH^q(\gamma_a)$. This computes the derived meaning stipulated in the item. More explicitly, [lem-sbc-filtered-colimit-cochain-homology] implies $H^q(\varinjlim_a C_a)\cong\varinjlim_aH^q(C_a)$ for any compatible diagram of integer-indexed $A$-complexes: apply its nonnegative version to the three-term complexes $C_a^{q-1}\to C_a^q\to C_a^{q+1}$ placed in degrees $0,1,2$, and take cohomology in degree $1$. Their middle cohomology is exactly $H^q(C_a)$ and their colimits are degreewise. These comparisons are natural for the original cocone and arrow maps. Hence for any other compatible representatives of the same derived diagram the Hom bijection of [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] gives a unique comparison to $QL_X,QL_Y$ inducing these canonical colimit cohomology identifications. Lift the inverse families to see that the comparisons are isomorphisms; injectivity makes them commute with every colimit leg and with $g$. This verifies independence from representatives with the prescribed arrows.

source.place: Tag 00DB (lemma-directed-colimit-exact); degreewise homology comparison of lem-sbc-filtered-colimit-cochain-homology and field Hom bijection.

proof.text: The degreewise continuity maps $\alpha^q,\beta^q$ of Step 3 define chain isomorphisms $L_X\to S(X)$ and $L_Y\to S(Y)$. Compose their localizations with $\theta_X,\theta_Y$ to obtain the canonical vertical comparisons $a:QL_X\to X$ and $b:QL_Y\to Y$. They have the required pullback cocone legs, since this holds on cohomology and the Hom bijection is injective. For every stage $a_0$, the limit equation in Step 6 says $\beta^q\iota_{a_0}H^q(\gamma_{a_0})=H^q(\gamma)\alpha^q\iota_{a_0}$. The colimit universal property therefore gives $\beta^qg^q=H^q(\gamma)\alpha^q$ for all $q$. Injectivity of the field Hom bijection yields $b\,Qg=\gamma\,a$ in $D(A)$, the required square. In particular its bottom arrow is the specified Kummer arrow: its maps are $H^q(\gamma)$ with the sign already fixed in Steps 5–6, and the Hom bijection permits no other arrow with those maps. If every $\gamma_a$ is invertible, the inverses of $S(\gamma_a)$ form a natural transformation in the opposite direction; their degreewise colimit is inverse to $g$. Thus $\gamma=b\,Qg\,a^{-1}$ is invertible. For $c=0$ the shift is zero and the class is the identity; empty supports give zero complexes, so these cases are included.
